content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis uses CMH test but sample size justification cites Chi-square test",
      "quote": "This sample size will yield >85% power to detect a treatment difference of 24% in the proportion of patients achieving IGA hand and foot (0, 1) at week 16 between placebo (10%) and dupilumab (34%) at a 2-sided significant level of 5% using Chi-square test",
      "page": 85,
      "section": "11.2 Justification of Sample Size",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size calculation is based on a Chi-square test, but the primary efficacy analysis specified in Section 11.4.3.1 uses a CMH test adjusting for stratification factors. This inconsistency may affect the actual power and should be reconciled.",
      "fix": "Align the sample size calculation with the planned primary analysis (CMH test) or justify the use of Chi-square approximation."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary estimand table is incomplete",
      "quote": "Table 2: Summary of Primary Estimand for Primary Endpoint Endpoint Intercurrent Event(s) Strategy Missing Data Handling Method Primary efficacy Composite strategy: Patient will be",
      "page": 86,
      "section": "11.4.3.1 Primary Efficacy Analysis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The table describing the primary estimand is cut off and does not specify the population, variable, summary measure, or complete intercurrent event strategies and missing data handling. This is a critical gap for estimand definition.",
      "fix": "Complete Table 2 with full details of the estimand attributes: population, variable, intercurrent event strategies, and missing data handling."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for secondary endpoint on WPAI and CIQ",
      "quote": "Change from baseline to week 16 in Work Productivity and Impairment (WPAI) and Classroom Impairment Questionnaire (CIQ)",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This secondary endpoint is listed but no corresponding statistical analysis method is described in the statistical plan. The plan should specify how this endpoint will be analyzed.",
      "fix": "Add a statistical analysis method for the WPAI and CIQ endpoint in Section 11.4."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for exploratory endpoints on EASI and IGA",
      "quote": "In patients with AD lesions on other parts of the body in addition to hands and feet; − Percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16 − Proportion of patients with IGA score of 0/1 at week 16 − Proportion of patients with EASI-75 at week 16",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "4.1.4 Exploratory Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Exploratory endpoints are listed but no analysis methods are provided in the statistical plan. The plan should include at least descriptive or inferential methods for these endpoints.",
      "fix": "Add analysis methods for exploratory endpoints in Section 11.4."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for clinical pharmacology and immunogenicity endpoints",
      "quote": "Trough concentration of functional dupilumab in serum at various time points • Incidence of treatment-emergent anti-drug antibody (ADA) and titer over time",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "These secondary endpoints are listed but no statistical analysis methods are described in the statistical plan. The plan should specify how these will be analyzed.",
      "fix": "Add analysis methods for pharmacokinetic and immunogenicity endpoints in Section 11.4."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for safety endpoint",
      "quote": "Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) through week 16",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint is listed but no statistical analysis method is described in the statistical plan. The plan should specify how TEAEs will be summarized and compared.",
      "fix": "Add a statistical analysis method for safety endpoints in Section 11.4."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of multiplicity for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "Secondary Endpoint for Efficacy: • Proportion of patients with improvement (reduction) of weekly average of daily hand and foot peak Pruritus NRS ≥4 from baseline to week 16",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical plan does not describe any multiplicity control strategy for the multiple secondary endpoints. This is a gap that could lead to inflated Type I error.",
      "fix": "Specify a multiplicity adjustment strategy (e.g., hierarchical testing, Bonferroni) for secondary endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing details on missing data handling for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "Handling of missing data due to the COVID-19 pandemic and any additional analyses required to investigate the impact of COVID-19 to understand estimated treatment effect and safety will be detailed in the SAP.",
      "page": 84,
      "section": "11 Statistical Plan",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The plan only mentions missing data handling for COVID-19 and defers to the SAP, but does not specify general missing data methods for secondary endpoints. This is a gap in the protocol.",
      "fix": "Include general missing data handling methods for all endpoints in the protocol or state that they will be detailed in the SAP."
    }
  ]
}
